title: Inside the Antenna: Cilia and Downstream Control

scenes.visual: Dark navy canvas (#0F172A). Large high-contrast title 'Inside the Antenna: Cilia and Downstream Control' in crisp white (size 44) centered above the same cell cross-section from the first film, with a pale-cyan (#A8DADC) antenna outline rising from its surface.

scenes.tts: The first film showed how Hedgehog turns off Patched so Smoothened keeps Glee whole. In vertebrate cells, where does that switch actually sit? And why can one Smoothened blocker both deform an embryo and shrink a skin tumour?
scenes.caption: The first film showed how Hedgehog turns off Patched so Smoothened keeps Gli whole. In vertebrate cells, where does that switch actually sit? And why can one Smoothened blocker both deform an embryo and shrink a skin tumour?
scenes.visual: Starts on the exact cell membrane and nucleus cross-section carried from the first film (coral Patched #E05A47, teal Smoothened #2AB7CA, violet-lavender Gli #9B72CF). Camera smoothly zooms slightly back to reveal a pale-cyan (#A8DADC) hair-like projection rising from the top of the cell, while a crisp magenta (#D81B60) drug wedge briefly glints beside Smoothened.
scenes.narration: The first film showed how Hedgehog turns off Patched so Smoothened keeps Gli whole. In vertebrate cells, where does that switch actually sit? And why can one Smoothened blocker both deform an embryo and shrink a skin tumour?

scenes.tts: Pull back from the plasma membrane to see that hair-like antenna. Most non-dividing vertebrate cells carry a single primary cilium. It does not beat like a motile whip. Motor shuttles called intraflagellar transport continuously build and maintain its microtubule core.
scenes.caption: Pull back from the plasma membrane to see that hair-like antenna. Most non-dividing vertebrate cells carry a single primary cilium. It does not beat like a motile whip. Motor shuttles called intraflagellar transport continuously build and maintain its microtubule core.
scenes.visual: The pale-cyan (#A8DADC) primary cilium fills 70% of the frame height, rising cleanly from the plasma membrane above the nucleus. Inside its shaft, parallel microtubule tracks carry tiny bright cargo shuttles smoothly up and down, labelled 'Intraflagellar transport (schematic)'. The shaft stands steady rather than whipping, with label 'Primary cilium'.
scenes.narration: Pull back from the plasma membrane to see that hair-like antenna. Most non-dividing vertebrate cells carry a single primary cilium. It does not beat like a motile whip. Motor shuttles called intraflagellar transport continuously build and maintain its microtubule core.

scenes.tts: In vertebrates, the Hedgehog switch runs inside this tiny compartment. Without Hedgehog, Patched sits along the ciliary membrane while Smoothened waits outside in the cell body. Meanwhile, trimming Glee, mainly the form called Glee three, into a repressor also depends on this cilium. Quiet cells actively silence target genes.
scenes.caption: In vertebrates, the Hedgehog switch runs inside this tiny compartment. Without Hedgehog, Patched sits along the ciliary membrane while Smoothened waits outside in the cell body. Meanwhile, trimming Gli, mainly the form called Gli3, into a repressor also depends on this cilium. Quiet cells actively silence target genes.
scenes.visual: Same primary cilium cross-section, labelled 'No Hedgehog'. Bright coral-red (#E05A47) Patched blocks line the ciliary membrane, keeping amber (#FFD166) sterol tokens out. Dim grey-teal (#2AB7CA) Smoothened blocks wait outside on the surrounding plasma membrane. Near the cilium, slate-blue (#6C8EBF) kinases and proteasome trim violet-lavender Gli3 into the deep-violet repressor, which drifts into the nucleus ('Genes OFF'). Empathy fix: Label 'Gli3 = main repressor form'.
scenes.narration: In vertebrates, the Hedgehog switch runs inside this tiny compartment. Without Hedgehog, Patched sits along the ciliary membrane while Smoothened waits outside in the cell body. Meanwhile, trimming Gli, mainly the form called Gli3, into a repressor also depends on this cilium. Quiet cells actively silence target genes.

scenes.tts: When Hedgehog binds Patched, the traffic reverses. Patched exits the primary cilium, and Smoothened moves inside and switches on. Full-length Glee proteins gather at the ciliary tip, escape trimming, and travel to the nucleus as activators. Both sides of Glee processing therefore depend on the cilium.
scenes.caption: When Hedgehog binds Patched, the traffic reverses. Patched exits the primary cilium, and Smoothened moves inside and switches on. Full-length Gli proteins gather at the ciliary tip, escape trimming, and travel to the nucleus as activators. Both sides of Gli processing therefore depend on the cilium.
scenes.visual: Same cilium cross-section, labelled '+ Hedgehog'. Warm-gold (#F5A623) Hedgehog docks on coral Patched; Patched slides out of the cilium and fades. Teal Smoothened glides smoothly up into the ciliary membrane and lights bright teal (#2AB7CA). Intact violet-lavender Gli bars accumulate at the rounded ciliary tip, then travel down into the nucleus ('Genes ON'). Subtle badge (size 28): 'Cilium needed for both forms'.

scenes.tts: Now trace the pathway as a chain of switches. Hedgehog turns off Patched, Patched holds back Smoothened, and Smoothened governs Glee inside the cilium. In a linear chain like this, a block or fault acting later overrides everything upstream of it.

scenes.visual: The cilium cross-section slides slightly left while a clean horizontal schematic chain builds across the upper frame in the exact same colours: gold 'Hedgehog' -| coral 'Patched' -| teal 'Smoothened (cilium)' -> violet 'Gli' -> 'Genes'. A moving highlight pulse travels left to right, then stops at a barrier marker placed downstream to show upstream arrows cannot bypass a downstream block.

scenes.tts: Watch that rule in an early vertebrate embryo. The forebrain starts with a single central eye field. Sonic hedgehog, a vertebrate Hedgehog, comes from the midline and switches on Smoothened to split that field in two. Now predict. The plant alkaloid cyclopamine locks Smoothened off while Sonic hedgehog still arrives. Will the eye field divide, or stay as one?

scenes.visual: Below the chain schematic, a clean schematic embryo forebrain silhouette appears at 65% height with one pale central eye oval above a warm-gold (#F5A623) midline Sonic hedgehog source. First, a brief preview shows normal midline gold signal splitting the oval toward left and right. Then it resets to one oval as a crisp magenta (#D81B60) wedge labelled 'Cyclopamine' snaps onto teal Smoothened in the chain above while gold Hedgehog still pulses from the midline. Bold top question banner (size 30): 'Smoothened locked off: divide or stay one?' Empathy fix: Label the midline source 'Sonic hedgehog (vertebrate Hh)'.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Question banner 'Smoothened locked off: divide or stay one?' stays crisp above the single pulsing eye field and magenta-locked Smoothened while a calm countdown ring fills over 4.5 seconds.

scenes.tts: It stays as a single central eye. Even though Hedgehog still turns off Patched, Smoothened sits downstream of both. Locking Smoothened off overrides the signal above it. Ewes grazing corn lily bore one-eyed lambs. The plant's cyclopamine later led researchers to Smoothened as a drug target.

scenes.visual: The central eye oval remains undivided in the middle of the forebrain schematic ('Single eye field'). Above it in the chain, gold Hedgehog switches coral Patched off, yet the signal halts sharply at the magenta-locked dim Smoothened block, leaving violet Gli trimmed and target genes off. Empathy fix: Show 'Corn lily → cyclopamine → Smoothened' as spoken.

scenes.tts: The same downstream rule explains a common human skin cancer. Most basal cell carcinomas lose Patched, leaving Smoothened running without Hedgehog. The drug vismodegib binds Smoothened and shuts it off. Because Smoothened acts downstream of Patched, blocking Smoothened silences the tumour pathway. But if a tumour's fault lies below Smoothened, vismodegib cannot stop it.

scenes.visual: Side-by-side comparison of two schematic tumour cells carrying the same colour map and pale-cyan cilia. Left ('Lost Patched'): coral Patched is missing (dashed outline), teal Smoothened glows ON; magenta (#D81B60) 'Vismodegib' wedge snaps into Smoothened, turning it dim and switching 'Genes OFF'. Right ('Downstream fault'): magenta vismodegib locks Smoothened dim, yet a glowing violet arrow downstream bypasses it and keeps 'Genes ON'. Empathy fix: Right panel label: 'Fault below Smoothened: drug fails'.

scenes.tts: Notice how location and order unite the whole story. The primary cilium gathers Patched, Smoothened, and Glee into one signalling hub. By contrast, most fly cells run this pathway without any cilium. Along that chain, downstream steps override upstream ones. In vertebrates, the cilium houses the switch, and downstream steps decide.
